body:
Equipment orderbook extract. This is a synthetic October 2026 research record about the fictional Vertex Compute 600 MW Johor–Singapore expansion. All organisations, interviews, figures and quotations in this article are invented for the ResearchAgent demonstration. The geography is real; this document is not evidence about any real company or utility.

Fictional purchase orders reserve transformers and switchgear for the first 240 MW of Vertex capacity.

Only 240 of the announced 600 MW has a confirmed energisation slot before 2028.

Substation works for the remaining phases have slipped 14 months beyond the earlier fictional programme.

This alternative fictional open dataset includes a published operator schedule alongside equipment orders. It matches connection records to campus phase identifiers and separates confirmed slots from applications. The added schedule answers the material operating date question using accessible evidence. The full programme remains commercially supported, but only partial capacity has a confirmed early slot. Readers do not need a premium report to establish this boundary in the alternative scenario. All records and operator names remain invented.

The record separates an announced plan from an observed milestone. Its authors keep the underlying unit of measurement visible and avoid treating a commercial commitment as proof of physical completion. A signed order, an available component and an operating building represent different stages of the same programme. Readers should compare records on their stated scope rather than add unlike quantities together. The article makes no claim that a supplier can remove every dependency outside its contract. It describes the evidence available in this fictional snapshot, not a guarantee of future performance. Changes after the snapshot would require another dated record and a fresh comparison.

The snapshot date is part of the evidence boundary. Earlier intentions may explain why an order was placed, but they do not replace the current record. The authors recommend retaining document provenance when comparing milestones across reporting families.
